bullets.text: THE RESHAPE: node_classes/_charter+why.json says a class defines 'its invariant and its VARIABLE GATE-SET' and 'a pipeline is just the gate-set on a node-class'. Read that way, 'device' is not a class — it names no gate-set. All five registered classes name a distinct prove_gate; device would inherit code-seam's. Akien's TOOLS intuition is right that a category is missing, but the missing thing is a SECOND AXIS, not a node_class and not a folder.

The compound strings are the proof that two axes are jammed into one field: cairn-web_server says 'code-seam (a spine device by role...)' and cairn-harbor_master says 'code-seam (device by role...)'. Two authors independently wrote BOTH axes into the one field they had.

Nothing in the system branches on the improvised parentheticals — (domain), (instrument), (gate), (stage) — while everything branches on the registered classes, because /sorted transcribes the class's gate-set into gates_bound at cast. The load-bearing half and the decorative half are now separable, which is what this design step needed.

members_so_far is stale across the whole registry: code-seam records ONE member against 38 charters and 13 self-declared devices. Nothing maintains it, and no door writes it — a registry that no longer knows its own membership cannot answer 'which lots are still unexcavated' (Law 9).

signal.verbatim: approve — the second axis is the complexity axis: tool/machine/device. Already settled. Tools are self-contained (a hammer). Machines are compound units using tools and other machines. Devices are top-level components. The parentheticals and members_so_far are dead weight.

bullets.text: The collision resolves rather than deadlocks: cairn/base's stated why is the UNIFORM INTROSPECTION SURFACE — one protocol for the tester and the web UI — and that is precisely the axis Akien named. Inheritance was the delivery mechanism, not the value. So BaseDevice loses its claim to define device-ness and keeps its job; that is the distinction to record at both ends.

If device-ness is decided at the shim, BaseShim is the load-bearing class and BaseDevice the optional one — an inversion of the current ordering that has to be checked against the spine before it is asserted.

The one measurement available immediately and not yet run: import_sieve's importers_of over cairn/base/device.py, to see who actually consumes BaseDevice. Running it before the edit is the whole point of this node — answering it by reading would repeat the defect that produced it.

RULING ORDER, recorded so it is not rediscovered: base-device first (it defines what 'device' means), then tools (which decides whether runtime role is an axis and what its values are), then alarms (which consumes both to ask whether trouble is one).

signal.verbatim: approve — a device is a first-class component: its own process, its own shim. No machine has a shim. The shim is what makes it a device, not the class it inherits.

bullets.text: This design step's first finding is a DEPENDENCY, not an answer: 'should trouble be a device' resolves to 'should trouble get a shim' if the base-device node's ruling holds. These two nodes were born from one conversation and cannot be cast independently — the alarms node is downstream of the base-device node.

The clear path is the load-bearing half and it has three requirements already written in trouble's charter — identify the recipient, refuse a clear that names no change, write through trouble's own door — none of which is measured as existing today.

The display half is the part most likely to be waste: both live troubles are printed in the session-open banner at every single session open and have stayed live anyway. A pane that only shows them repeats a surface that already failed to move them.
'Only the recipient clears it' presumes a named recipient, and whether that is a recorded field on a trouble or an inference made by a reader is unmeasured — Law 6 needs it recorded.
